title: Integral Borel cohomology through degree three and its second filtration for the order-twelve dihedral action on the hexagonal torus
author: Kiyonori Gomi
source_title: Twists on the Torus Equivariant under the 2-Dimensional Crystallographic Point Groups
difficulty_reason: Computing this Borel equivariant cohomology requires a stabilizer-sensitive cell decomposition and two Mayer-Vietoris sequences with explicit character restriction maps. Recovering the Leray-Serre filtration additionally requires a nontrivial integral module extension and the multiplication-by-three map in group cohomology. These constructions and their compatibility exceed a routine application of the spectral sequence or ordinary qualifying topology.
source_version: Official SIGMA 13 (2017) article 014, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2017.014; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.note: The complete p6m computation in Section4.5 is read, including the explicit hexagonal D6-CW decomposition, both Mayer-Vietoris restriction maps on character bases, free two-cell excision, the integral D6-module extension with composition equal to multiplication by three, and its Leray-Serre filtration computation. Theorems4.11 and4.14 form one cohomology computation, not two counted variants. General fixed-point splitting and sign-coefficient lemmas4.1-4.3 and5.4-5.6 are bundled. Lemma5.6 gives the two natural exact sequences and a worked coefficient calculation; the remaining low-degree cases are expressly routine use of those sequences, retained as the author's bounded calculation rather than independently expanded. Known finite-group integral cohomology is cited background. No global wallpaper table or equivariant stable-splitting Lemma4.4 is selected or required. Literal D4 in the ambient character group at the end of Lemma4.9 is a local notation slip: the immediately defined subgroup, its characters and all maps are D2; original bytes remain unchanged.

statement_scope: Only the hexagonal lattice Pi=Z(1,0)+Z(1/2,sqrt(3)/2), acted on by C=rotation through pi/3 and sigma=reflection in the first coordinate axis, with D6 of order12. Theorems4.11 and4.14 together give H0=Z,H1=0,H2=(Z/2)^2,H3=(Z/2)^2 and F2H3=Z/2. No other wallpaper action, twisted coefficients or global table is selected.
editorial_warning: Original author notation is preserved. The incidental D4 in Lemma4.9 character-group display denotes the explicitly defined D2 subgroup; the listed characters and restriction maps specify the calculation. Lemma5.6 expressly leaves other low-degree exact-sequence cases as routine calculations after a worked case.
